# BINDING CONSISTENCY LEDGER — Dutch Listening Pod (15 Scenes)

## 1. TRANSLITERATION
Transliteration: not needed — names stay as written.

## 2. PRICES
Eight pound forty → acht euro veertig
Half pint → drieënhalve euro (or "drieënhalve" for a vaasje/half-litre in NL standard)
Twelve pound fifty → twaalf euro vijftig
Two pounds → twee euro
One pound → een euro
General coffee/drink prices: €2,50–€3,50
Beer (pint equiv./vaasje): €4,00–€5,00
Wine (glass): €5,00–€7,00
Water (glass): gratis or €1,00
Food (sandwich/light): €6,00–€9,00
Food (main course): €14,00–€22,00

## 3. TARGET-LANGUAGE NAME
**Nederlands** (the standard everyday word Dutch speakers use for their own language)

## 4. RECURRING LINES

| Canonical | Dutch Rendering |
|-----------|-----------------|
| Good morning | Goedemorgen |
| Good afternoon | Goedemiddag |
| Good evening | Goedenavond |
| Goodbye / See you later | Tot ziens / Doei |
| What can I get you? | Wat kan ik voor je doen? / Wat mag het zijn? |
| Please | Alsjeblieft / 'Stblieft |
| Thank you (very much) | Dank je (wel) / Dankjewel |
| You're welcome | Graag gedaan |
| Excuse me | Pardon / Sorry |
| I'm learning Dutch | Ik leer Nederlands |
| Could I pay by card? | Kan ik pinnen? |
| Do you have contactless? | Hebben jullie contactloos betalen? |
| Could I see the menu? | Mag ik de kaart zien? |
| Would you like to sit-in or takeaway? | Wil je dit meenemen of hier eten? |
| Are you eating tonight? | Eten jullie vanavond? |
| Would you like anything else? | Kan ik nog iets voor je doen? / Nog iets? |
| Is everything alright? | Gaat het goed met je? / Smaakt het goed? |
| The bill, please | De rekening graag |
| Thank you, you've been very helpful | Dank je, je bent erg behulpzaam |

## 5. REGISTER

**Customer ↔ Service staff** (café, bar, shop, pharmacy, hotel, taxi): **jij/je** — standard informal Dutch, even with strangers. Politeness via efficient directness, not elaborate honorifics.

**Stranger ↔ Stranger** (street directions, first meeting): **jij/je** — default. Only shift to **u** if customer appears notably elderly or interaction is formal (hotel reception, pharmacy consultation for sensitive health issue).

**Friend ↔ Friend** / **Learner ↔ Friend helping with language practice**: **jij/je** — informal, warm, natural.

**Politeness markers**: Low-key. Alsjeblieft/dank je wel carry both "please" and "thank you" weight. No elaborate apology chains. "Pardon" or brief "sorry" for attention-getting; direct requests ("Mag ik…?") preferred over softening ("Would you terribly mind…?").
